conditional_clauses.note: Insurance covenant, added once the engagement's value or term reaches elevated exposure
Audit, information and escalation rights, included when the user supplied any of them.
Dated milestones. Included when the user's stated risk is missed deadlines.
Progress reporting, the mechanism by which a missed deadline is seen before it is missed.
Acceptance criteria and rejection. Included when the user's stated risk is work below the agreed standard.

IP_OWNERSHIP_001 is already forced in by the hardening policy and vests the deliverables in the Client, so an assignment clause would only repeat it. What a user worried about ownership does not otherwise get is the warranty that the work does not infringe someone else's rights, which is what this adds.

Exclusivity during the term only. NDA_NON_COMPETE_001 was tried first and pulled in the NDA confidential-information scope clause with Disclosing/Receiving Party roles, which do not belong in a consultancy agreement.
Handover on exit, included when the user's stated risk is the consultant leaving mid-project.
What is reimbursable and what is not. Included when the user's stated risk is unexpected costs.
Change control, so scope growth is priced rather than absorbed.

mandatory_legal_checks: TDS under S.194J (10%) applies to professional/consulting fees — address in payment clause
GST at 18% on consulting services — invoice compliance required
Copyright Act S.19 — IP assignment must be in writing
Independent contractor clause critical — EPF/ESI reclassification risk

variant_clauses.note: How the engagement is billed. SERVICE_PAYMENT_001 points at a fee schedule; these state the actual mechanics, which is what a dispute turns on.
